articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Launch Sees Surge in Late-Night Food Deliveries
articles.summary: The massive success of Grand Theft Auto VI has led to a surge in late-night food deliveries, with gamers taking advantage of special deals from delivery apps.
articles.content: The massive success of Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI has led to a peculiar challenge for gamers worldwide: how to satisfy their hunger without interrupting their gaming session. To address this issue, delivery apps have anticipated the demand for one-handed snacks. Uber Eats, in particular, has prepared special deals that cater to gamers who don't want to put down their controllers. Among the offers are buy-one-get-one McNuggets at McDonald's, boneless wings at Wingstop, and Whopper Jr. burgers at Burger King - all designed to be consumed with ease while gaming. These promotions were part of a broader effort by Uber Eats to support gamers on launch night. According to Andrew Macdonald, President and COO of Uber, the company deliberately chose food deals that could be enjoyed with one hand in mind. This move was intended to enable fans to focus on the game without interruption. As gamers took advantage of these offers, Uber Eats saw a significant surge in orders between midnight and 5 a.m. on launch night, with Miami experiencing a notable increase of over 30% compared to the prior two Thursdays. Miami's late-night food delivery boom continued unabated as DoorDash reported a significant surge in orders for popular comfort foods. Between 9 p.m. and 2 a.m. ET, DoorDash saw a substantial increase in demand for chips, burgers, fries, and pizza, each rising more than 10% compared to the average of the six prior Wednesdays. Energy drinks also experienced a notable spike, with orders jumping by over 20%. Philadelphia, Detroit, and Atlanta joined Miami in seeing double-digit increases in late-night orders, according to DoorDash's data dashboard. DoorDash's own numbers show that gaming gear was also flying off the shelves, with controllers and gaming accessories seeing a staggering 450% increase in sales. HDMI cables followed closely behind, rising by 440%. Meanwhile, GTA VI fans were eagerly awaiting the game's launch, with searches for the title on DoorDash's app skyrocketing by more than 940% in the week leading up to its release. As the gaming community came together to celebrate the highly anticipated game, some players opted to watch rather than play. According to Streams Charts, GTA VI drew more livestream watch time in its first two days than any other game had in its entire launch week. GTA VI's cultural significance was not lost on DoorDash's marketing team, with Vice President Gina Igwe calling the game "more than a game launch and a moment that fans have been waiting years for. The gaming community's enthusiasm for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) extended beyond the virtual world to the real-life dinner table, as food delivery companies capitalized on the hype surrounding the game's launch. Twitch viewership soared during the launch period, with a 61% increase in total watch time compared to the two days prior. This surge in interest came at the expense of other popular games like World of Warcraft and Counter-Strike, which saw their Twitch watch times drop by about 31%. Fortnite also suffered a significant decline on YouTube, losing 60% of its viewers. The gaming community's eating habits were not immune to the GTA VI phenomenon. Food chains like Popeyes got in on the action by introducing a limited-time Spice City sandwich, named after the game's setting. Players were encouraged to order through the restaurant's app while taking breaks from their gaming sessions. Other companies joined in on the fun, with McDonald's starting to take delivery orders directly on Discord, a popular chat platform used by gamers. DoorDash partnered with Wendy's and The Cheesecake Factory to offer special deals, while Grubhub gave its first 1,000 customers $10 off their orders. Sensor Tower, an analytics firm, predicts that GTA VI will generate over 50 million additional visits to U.S. food delivery and restaurant apps in the game's first 30 days. This influx of new customers is expected to have a significant impact on the companies involved. The actual dollar figure spent on takeout during launch night remains unclear, with neither company providing a specific estimate. However, based on their earnings reports, Uber and DoorDash handled around $680 million in delivery orders worldwide each day in the third quarter. Assuming that late-night hours account for about 10% of this total, and considering that GTA VI's launch may have boosted these orders by 10-25%, the additional spending could range from $7 million to $17 million. The massive influx of money spent on Grand Theft Auto VI's launch night was not a sudden injection into the economy, but rather a reallocation of existing funds from other leisure activities. According to economists, events like this one typically see people rearranging their free time spending habits, rather than generating new revenue. As Victor Matheson, an economist at the College of the Holy Cross, noted, People just rearrange how they're spending their free time." This shift in priorities likely contributed to the significant increase in gaming-related expenditures. Restaurants also felt the impact, with a substantial number of workers calling in sick or missing shifts on launch day. Data from scheduling platform Harri revealed that 92% more missed restaurant shifts occurred on November 19 compared to the previous week, resulting in one in 14 shifts going unworked. Furthermore, sales at these restaurants declined by less than 2%. The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S had a relatively minor impact on office attendance and coworking space usage. Industrious, a coworking company with over 250 U.S. locations, reported that Wi-Fi logins fell about 5% on launch day compared to the previous three Thursdays, indicating that many employees chose to stay home and play instead of going into work. At the other end of the pitch, Koln goalkeeper Jonas Urbig had a relatively quiet game until he was called upon to make several vital saves to keep his team in the match. Despite being largely a spectator for long periods due to Bayern's possession dominance, Urbig proved himself to be reliable when needed. The Bayern team's possession dominance continued unabated as they maintained a whopping 71% share of the ball throughout the match. Aleksandar Pavlovic played a crucial role in this endeavor, working tirelessly to provide a platform for his more advanced teammates to flourish on the pitch. Meanwhile, Michael Olise struggled to make his mark on the game, failing to create any significant scoring opportunities despite being given a chance to shine on the right wing. The Frenchman's performance was marred by an injury that forced him off the pitch at half-time, making way for Tim Binder to take over and try to turn things around. Kimmich continued to set the pace for Bayern, his impressive passing range and vision allowing him to dictate the tempo of the game from midfield. His long-range efforts were a testament to his ability to unlock the defense, even if his 22nd-minute shot did not quite test the keeper as he had hoped. Lennart Karl continued to be a driving force for Bayern, taking on a more central role in their creative efforts throughout the match. His constant pressure on the Koln defense led to several attempts on goal, including one that forced a save from the keeper in the 54th minute. Nathaniel Brown's performance was a highlight of the evening, as he consistently threatened the Koln backline with his precise technique and quick thinking on the field. The absence of Harry Kane was keenly felt after his early exit due to injury, which left Bayern struggling to find their rhythm in the match. The German giants were searching for a way to bypass Koln's defensive shape, but Binder's efforts were thwarted by their solid organization. The introduction of Kim Min-Jae in the 70th minute provided Bayern with a much-needed boost at the back, as he helped stabilize the defense and prevented Koln from scoring late on. Jamal Musiala was brought on for the final 20 minutes to bring some creativity to the game, but his two late chances were squandered due to poor finishing. Despite his energetic display, Bayern still struggled to find a way past Koln's defense. The Bavarians dominated possession throughout the match, but their inability to convert it into goals was a major concern, especially with Harry Kane's injury now casting a shadow over their campaign. articles.title: French Court Hands Prison Sentences to Police Officers Involved in 2020 Beating of Michel Zecler
articles.summary: A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers involved in the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler, sparking hope among advocates for greater transparency and accountability within law enforcement.
articles.content: A French court has made a rare move in handing down prison sentences to three police officers involved in the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked widespread outrage and put a spotlight on issues of police violence and racism in France. The officers had accused Zecler, now 47, of not wearing a face mask during the Covid-19 pandemic, but their actions were widely condemned as excessive and racist. This case has reignited debates over systemic police brutality, with victims and researchers pointing to a long-standing problem that authorities often downplay as isolated incidents. The court's decision marks a rare instance where police officers have been held accountable for their actions in such cases, sparking hope among advocates for greater transparency and accountability within law enforcement. The case has also sparked renewed scrutiny of the relationship between police and minority communities in France. Zecler's treatment at the hands of the officers was severe enough to warrant significant prison time for two of them, who received five-year sentences, including suspended terms, while a third officer will serve one year with an ankle tag. The recent sentencing of Paris police officers for their role in beating a Black man has sparked renewed criticism of systemic racism within France's law enforcement agencies. Campaigners and rights groups have long argued that ethnic minorities face harsher treatment at the hands of French police compared to white people, and this case is seen as further evidence of this disparity. The incident, which took place on November 21, 2020, outside a Paris studio where the victim was working, saw him being stopped by officers who accused him of not wearing a face mask and suspected cannabis use. A review of the security footage from the studio revealed that police pushed Zecler into his office and subjected him to a violent assault that left him with serious injuries. A guilty verdict in an alleged police brutality case is a rare occurrence in France, where most such incidents are handled internally. This was evident in two recent cases that made it to court: one involving a French policeman who shot and killed 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk outside Paris in June 2023, and another in which three officers were given suspended jail sentences for inflicting irreversible harm on a black man, Theo Luhaka, during a stop-and-search in 2017. The verdicts came after video footage contradicted the police's account of events in both cases. The shooting of Nahel Merzouk sparked nationwide protests, highlighting concerns about police conduct and accountability. Meanwhile, the suspended sentences handed down to the officers who harmed Theo Luhaka were seen as a rare acknowledgment of police wrongdoing. Young men perceived as Arab, black, or from North Africa are disproportionately affected by police stops, being four times more likely to be targeted than others, according to France's rights chief. They are also 12 times more likely to face harsher measures during these interactions, including invasive searches, a finding based on a survey of over 5,000 people. articles.title: Gravity Can Act as Repulsive Force at Small Scales
articles.summary: Two independent research teams have found evidence that quantum effects can cause gravity to act as a repulsive force, pushing objects apart rather than pulling them together.
articles.content: Scientists have made a groundbreaking discovery that could potentially defy one of the fundamental laws of physics: gravity. According to Einstein's theory of relativity, gravity is always an attractive force, pulling objects with mass towards each other. This phenomenon is what keeps the moon in orbit around Earth and causes apples to fall from trees. However, at very small scales, where quantum effects come into play, there has been a lack of understanding about how gravity behaves. Two independent research teams have now found evidence that quantum effects can cause gravity to act as a repulsive force, pushing objects apart rather than pulling them together. This contradicts the long-held assumption that gravity is always attractive.
